entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Barisone III of Torres was a brief but significant Giudice of Logudoro from 1232 until his death in 1236. Born to Marianus II, he succeeded his father and played a minor role in the complex web of medieval politics in Sardinia.

As Giudice, Barisone III oversaw the administration of the region, which was a hotbed of conflict between the Republic of Pisa and the Republic of Genoa. He also dealt with the ongoing struggle between the Ghibellines and Guelphs, two factions vying for control of the island.

Despite his short tenure, Barisone III left a lasting legacy in the region, with his family going on to play a significant role in Sardinian politics for centuries to come. His story serves as a reminder of the complex and often brutal nature of medieval politics.

The legacy of Barisone III can be seen in the many fortified castles and churches that dot the Sardinian landscape, testaments to the enduring power of the island's medieval rulers.
